newsitem.title: INDIA: India rupee sways against dlr, forward premia jump.
newsitem.headline: India rupee sways against dlr, forward premia jump.

text.p: The forward dollar was in the limelight in India's inter-bank forex market on Friday after two days of hectic action in the spot dollar market, dealers said.
"People were paying (premia for forward dollar) madly today," said the chief dealer at a state-run bank. "There was near-panic in the market," he said.
May dollar was quoted at a premium of 1.65/1.68 rupees at close of trading, down from the day's high of 1.70/1.75 rupees and up from the day's opening level of 1.54/1.57 rupees.
"It was crazy, there was no real reason (for such a rise)," said a dealer. Most dealers attributed the sharp rise to players cutting down their large forward commitments.
Some dealers said stop loss limits were crossed.
A reversal of sentiment in the domestic money market with overnight call rates breaching the 11.0 percent resistance level on Thursday also contributed to the sentiment, dealers said.
A 20 billion rupee bond auction scheduled for November 26 also vitiated the sentiment, they said. Banks had received premia in the recent past looking at the easy call rates.
The six-month annualised forward premium ended at 8.77 percent on Friday, down from the previous 8.05 percent.
"Unless something happens to reverse the sentiment, I don't see much downside in forwards," a dealer said.
The spot dollar which opened at 35.76/78 on Friday, closed at 35.77/78 and swayed both ways during the day, dealers said.
The first major bid came from long-term lending bank ICICI which bought a substantial amount to pay interest on an overseas loan. ICIC bought upto 35.7950 level.
A leading Calcutta bank's entry dragged the rupee to 35.8250 level, which triggered lot of corporate dollar selling, dealers said. The rupee swayed both ways until it closed at 35.77/78.
Approaching month-end dollar demand and reduced dollar supply on Friday arrested the rupee's recovery, one dealer said.
